sentences.text: The Substation Operator maintains the Offshore Substation within approved operating limits and follows current switching instructions.
At the start of each shift, the operator reviews alarms, active restrictions, equipment status, and handover notes.
Routine rounds cover room temperature, ventilation, water ingress, lighting, access control, and visible signs of damage.
The operator checks Main Transformer temperatures, cooling equipment, oil indications, and abnormal noise against established limits.
The Export Cable Monitor is reviewed for trends or alarms that require escalation to the Control Engineer.
The Grid Interface Relay is checked for healthy indications and consistency with the approved grid operating state.
The SCADA Gateway displays are compared with local indications when equipment status is uncertain.
The Control Engineer investigates unexplained discrepancies before operating personnel rely on remote indications.
The Work Permit Portal is checked to confirm that active work authorizations and isolation boundaries remain current.
The operator verifies that personnel access records are consistent with the planned work and current site occupancy.
The Fire Detection Panel is checked for healthy status, active faults, and unobstructed access to response equipment.
The Emergency Generator produces the Start Test Trace during its scheduled functional test.
The operator confirms fuel level, starting battery condition, ventilation, and readiness of the Emergency Generator for loss of normal supply.
Foxglove is exercised under the approved test procedure to confirm reliable backup starting and stable output.
The operator records test results and raises a defect promptly if the Emergency Generator fails to start or sustain its required load.
The Cybersecurity Gateway uses the revocation receipt to support access control during routine account and session reviews.
Switching is performed only by authorized personnel using approved instructions and positive confirmation of equipment identity.
Before operating a breaker or isolator, the operator verifies the required clearances and confirms that affected parties are informed.
If a protection alarm, abnormal electrical condition, or loss of critical monitoring occurs, the operator limits further switching and escalates the condition.
The operator places the Offshore Substation in Substation Degraded when required by operating procedures and communicates the resulting restrictions.
The Grid Dispatcher is notified when a condition could affect export capability or compliance with grid instructions.
The Electrical Technician supports fault diagnosis and maintenance under the applicable work authorization and isolation controls.
The Shore Control Room receives concise status updates, including operating limitations and the expected time of the next review.
Shift records capture inspections, alarms, tests, switching actions, defects, and handover items so that decisions remain traceable.
